transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Recording: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (AetherOps HO ML), Carlos Ruiz (AetherOps Infra), Priya Shah (AetherOps Product)

Summary: Quick review of pilot token economics, caching results from last week's KV cache test, discussion of batching tradeoffs for low-latency routes, and alignment on next validation steps. Team agreed to run a focused throughput benchmark on Redwood dedicated-sim and to exchange raw token burn logs.

Topics: token/sec/$, batching vs latency, prefix/KV cache savings, quantization impact, dedicated vs hosted cost predictability, security packet follow-up

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: okay welcome everybody, thanks for joining. we are on the weekly check-in for the aetherops pilot, is everyone here?
[00:05] Maya Lin: yeah hey alex, maya here. carlos and priya are on.
[00:08] Carlos Ruiz: hey hi.
[00:12] Alex Rivera: awesome, quick agenda — results from last week's KV caching experiment, tokens per second per dollar numbers, and then samir will walk through some batching sims. we'll close with next steps. sound good?
[00:20] Priya Shah: yep sounds good.
[00:25] Samir Patel: hey just a note, i pulled the cache numbers again, there's some weird noise on one of the routes — i think a mismatch in the prefix keys, so savings look higher than reality in route three.
[00:36] Maya Lin: yeah we saw that too, route three has a lot of template variation, so the prefix hit rate is lower in prod than in the test set.
[00:44] Alex Rivera: okay that's useful. samir, can you run the same test but with the broader prompt set maya sent yesterday? that should surface real hit rates.
[00:52] Samir Patel: yeah i'll kick that off after the call. i also modeled tokens/sec per dollar for three configs — hosted small, dedicated gpus with q4 quantization, and dedicated mixed with prefix cache.
[01:05] Maya Lin: quick question on the q4 numbers — did you assume per-token speedup or just cost delta from the quantization?
[01:12] Samir Patel: both — q4 reduces memory so we can run bigger batches which increases tokens/sec, but single-token latency is slightly worse on some backends. i included both effects.
[01:24] Carlos Ruiz: for our user flows the 99th p90 latency matters. we can't have a 150ms jump for interactive routes.
[01:31] Alex Rivera: agreed. remember we can do mixed routing: keep critical interactive routes on hosted low-latency model variant and route batchy inference to dedicated quantized replicas. that keeps end-user latency tight while saving on bulk.
[01:46] Priya Shah: that's the pattern we were hoping for. how much savings are we seeing though? what's tokens per dollar for the hybrid?
[01:54] Samir Patel: in the sim, hybrid delivered ~2.3x tokens/sec per dollar vs all-hosted baseline for our sample workload, but that assumes a 40% cache hit rate. if prefix hit drops to 15% that goes down to ~1.4x.
[02:12] Maya Lin: hmm our prod hit looks around 22% on Friday's run. so we'd be in the middle.
[02:19] Alex Rivera: also important — these sims didn't include KV cache warmup effects across user sessions. we often see hit rate climb after 24-48h as KV warms in steady state.
[02:32] Carlos Ruiz: how reliable is that warmup? our traffic has a daily churn, many ephemeral sessions.
[02:38] Samir Patel: good point. warmup helps on sustained workloads; for high-churn apps the caching benefit is less. i put a churn parameter into the next sim.
[02:47] Priya Shah: can you show the sim quickly? even a rough slide?
[02:50] Samir Patel: sure, sharing screen — okay table here: baseline tokens/sec/$ for hosted is 1x, dedicated-quant is 2.1x, hybrid-with-40%-cache becomes 2.3x. then i show sensitivity: 40% hit -> 2.3x, 25% -> 1.7x, 10% -> 1.1x.
[03:12] Maya Lin: that sensitivity chart is helpful. our top-10 prompts are heavy on variable user text so maybe lower end.
[03:19] Alex Rivera: maya, can you paste the top-10 prompts in the slack thread after this call so samir can re-run with exact distributions?
[03:26] Maya Lin: yes i'll do that.
[03:30] Carlos Ruiz: another factor — KV cache egress and mem pressure on our side when we run private. there was a comment last week about memory spikes under heavy batch.
[03:39] Samir Patel: memory spikes come from large batches building big KV caches; we can cap the KV window or tune cache TTL to guard memory. that does reduce hit rate slightly.
[03:49] Priya Shah: so it's a tradeoff: cap cache -> lower hit -> higher cost. keep cache -> risk spikes.
[03:55] Alex Rivera: exactly. that's why we want to run a dedicated-sim benchmark that mirrors your session churn and batch windows. it's the single best signal.
[04:05] Maya Lin: timeline? can you run that this week?
[04:08] Alex Rivera: yes we can start tomorrow. samir, can you provision the sim and run 5k mixed requests?
[04:14] Samir Patel: yep i'll queue that, expecting finish by tuesday. i'll also vary cache TTL and batch max size.
[04:22] Carlos Ruiz: please include p95/p99 latency breakdown — not just avg tokens/sec.
[04:26] Samir Patel: will do.
[04:30] Priya Shah: curious about quantization quality regressions — how did q4 hold up on our evals?
[04:35] Samir Patel: the automated evals showed minor hit on answer quality for one prompt type (the multi-step reasoning one). we can do a small canary on production-like traffic and fallback to the full-precision variant when quality dips.
[04:47] Maya Lin: fallback policy sounds good. do you have an automated rollback?
[04:51] Alex Rivera: yes the rollout canary supports immediate fallback to a pinned FP32 variant. it's in the pilot runbook i shared last week (link in chat).
[04:58] Carlos Ruiz: about security — we're still waiting on your SOC2 docs and SSO integration guide, that blocks any private deployment testing.
[05:06] Alex Rivera: noted, i'll send the packet today. it includes SOC2, ISO snapshot, SSO SAML steps, and a network diagram.
[05:12] Priya Shah: also need clarification on data retention for logs and redaction options.
[05:16] Alex Rivera: we have configurable retention and audit logs — samir will include retention knobs in the runbook appendix.
[05:22] Samir Patel: yep i'll add a note and link to the console settings.
[05:26] Maya Lin: one more item — bursting. if we keep dedicated we want predictable bursting behavior. how does Redwood handle spikes?
[05:33] Samir Patel: dedicated clusters can be configured with burst capacity to use shared-hosted fallback for overflow; policy-based routing will send non-critical traffic to cheaper, lower-priority capacity.
[05:44] Carlos Ruiz: what's the cost hit when it falls back to shared-hosted during bursts, roughly?
[05:48] Alex Rivera: depends on volume, but typical blended tokens/sec/$ drops to somewhere between the dedicated price and hosted baseline; we'll model that in the benchmark output.
[05:57] Priya Shah: are we leaning toward dedicated then? from product perspective we like determinism.
[06:01] Maya Lin: infra leans dedicated for SLAs, product worried about cost.
[06:05] Alex Rivera: that's the usual dance. the dedicated-hybrid with caching and batching usually gives the best control: you pay for steady pipes, and route bursty, cheap traffic elsewhere.
[06:17] Samir Patel: i want to flag one weird artifact from our last run: the route with lots of short prompts actually had worse tokens/sec/$ when batched aggressively because of decoder memory friction — basically the inference throughput decreased past a certain batch size.
[06:30] Carlos Ruiz: interesting. so batching isn't purely beneficial.
[06:33] Samir Patel: right, there's a knee where token parallelism helps until memory and KV ops become the bottleneck. i'll include that knee point per route in my sim.
[06:43] Priya Shah: ok actionable items then: samir runs the sim, we share prompts, alex sends docs. any other asks?
[06:50] Maya Lin: can you also share the raw token burn logs, not just aggregated CSV? we want to run our own analysis.
[06:55] Alex Rivera: yes we'll share raw logs with obfuscated user ids.
[06:59] Carlos Ruiz: and please note network egress numbers so we can map to our cloud charges.
[07:04] Alex Rivera: will include that.
[07:08] Priya Shah: timeline recap?
[07:10] Alex Rivera: Samir finishes sim by Tue 26th, Alex sends SOC2/docs by Fri 22nd, Maya shares prompts by Fri 21st, Redwood to share token logs by Fri 21st. workshop scheduled 25th pending availability.
[07:25] Maya Lin: sounds good. thanks all.
[07:28] Alex Rivera: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in slack and update the CRM.
[07:32] (end)

Notes and references: pilot runbook link (shared in chat), preliminary token burn csv link: https://redwood.ai/pilot/aetherops/token-burn.csv (placeholder), security packet link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.zip (placeholder).

End of transcript.
